title: Dummy Backend: Profile Viewer
description: Practice fetching data from the dummy backend using useEffect, managing loading and error states, and wiring a refresh button.

steps.title: Set Up Profile State
steps.explanation: You will fetch the demo user from the dummy backend (GET /api/profile). To handle the full async lifecycle, set up three pieces of state: the profile object, a loading flag, and an error message. This mirrors a common interview pattern: data / loading / error.
steps.task: Import useState from React and create three state variables in DummyProfile: 1) profile (initially null) to hold the user from /api/profile, 2) loading (initially true), and 3) error (initially null).
hints: Start loading as true so the UI can show a spinner while the first request runs.
Keep profile as null initially; you will render conditionally when it exists.

steps.title: Fetch from /api/profile with useEffect
steps.explanation: Now wire the component to the dummy backend. Use useEffect with an empty dependency array so the fetch runs once on mount. Inside, call fetch('http://localhost:4000/api/profile'), check response.ok, parse JSON, and update profile state. Capture any failures in the error state and make sure loading is set to false when the request finishes.
steps.task: Import useEffect and create an effect that, on mount, asynchronously fetches from 'http://localhost:4000/api/profile'. On success, store the parsed JSON in profile and clear any previous error. On failure, store a helpful error message. Always set loading to false in a finally block.
hints: Define an async function inside useEffect (do not make the effect callback itself async).
Use a finally block to guarantee loading becomes false whether the request succeeds or fails.

steps.title: Render Loading, Error, and Profile States
steps.explanation: A polished UI clearly communicates each state of the request. Use early returns: if loading, show a loading message; if there is an error, show it; if there is no profile yet and no error, show a friendly empty state. When the profile is available, render a simple card with the user's name and role from the dummy backend.
steps.task: Update the DummyProfile JSX so that: 1) when loading is true, you render a div with text 'Loading profile...'; 2) when error has a value, you render 'Error: {error}'; 3) when profile is present, you render the user's name in a heading and their role in a paragraph; 4) if neither loading nor error nor profile is present, show a small 'No profile loaded.' message.
hints: Use early returns to keep the main return clean.
Access fields from the dummy backend object as profile.name and profile.role.
Make sure loading is checked before error, and error before profile.

steps.title: Add a Refresh Button Using a Reusable Loader
steps.explanation: Interviewers often add a follow‑up: 'Great, now make it refresh on demand.' Extract your fetch logic into a reusable loadProfile function and call it from both useEffect and a Refresh button. Be careful to reset loading and error appropriately so the UI stays consistent while the new request is in flight.
steps.task: Refactor your code so the fetch logic lives in a loadProfile function that you can call from both useEffect and a 'Refresh' button. When the button is clicked, start loading again, clear any previous error, and show the updated data when the request completes.
hints: Move the body of your async function inside useEffect into a separate loadProfile function.
Call loadProfile() inside useEffect on mount.
Use <button onClick={loadProfile}>Refresh</button> to trigger a new request.
